### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
This catalogue distinguishes test assertions from executed results.
No snapy binary or installed snapy package was used for this draft.
Report-only algebra checks run on CPU and import no snapy.
:::

The tests below support @sec-ch01-driver through @sec-ch01-dependencies. A tolerance copied from a test is a
specification, not a measured error. Missing tolerance rationale is retained as missing evidence rather than invented.

### Derivation

The derivations of @eq-ch01-stage-weight, @eq-ch01-stage-transfer and @eq-ch01-stage-dry are checked by the
report-only stage check. There is no independent verification-catalogue derivation.

### Numerical method

Read the test source, confirm its registration and device selection, then run a package built from the stated pin.
The flow in @fig-ch01-driver-flow separates stage execution from step acceptance. Test outcomes depend on build
options;
this source inventory is not a generated `ctest -N` list.

The restart runner uses two processes and checks the first resumed cycle against the uninterrupted run, then
checks termination at its configured cycle limit. The parallel redo test likewise requires a process group and
restores saved tensors exactly. The C++ multi-block exchange test uses two local blocks and sees both local and
remote neighbors, but checks floating values using library-default `allclose`. The Python exchange test uses four
local blocks in one process and exact equality for its selected neighbor slab; it does not inspect every face.

The scripted forcing tests are CPU source tests. The scalar and coordinate device fixture enumerates CPU and CUDA
in float32 and float64 and skips unavailable CUDA; it does not instantiate MPS. The long-line reconstruction test
compares float64 CPU/CUDA at lengths 32, 1024, 1025, 1030 and 1280 and also tests multiple lines. These are test
inputs at the pin, not successful-run counts. The import-path test exits with skip status 125 when the target
package path is absent. No CPU, CUDA or multi-rank snapy runtime pass is claimed in this catalogue.

Report-only checks `[C1]`, `[C2]` and `[C3]` have committed output. Symbolic residuals must be exactly zero.
The numerical transfer checks permit absolute error of 64 float64 machine epsilons times the larger of one
and the sum of absolute face transfers, allowing the short sequence of upwind products, differences and sums.
The dry-source branch checks use the same 64-epsilon scale for unit-sized examples. These are algebra checks,
not a substitute for an execution of the C++ branches or a convergence ladder.

### Limits

Dedicated evidence is missing for split-source ghost freshness, initialization-versus-restart ghost equivalence,
all `part` extension combinations, MPS dispatch, and the imported dependency stack at this pin. No runtime
switch-combination coverage is added to @sec-ch12-matrix. Before publication, run the selected CPU tests with
verified package origin, record their outcomes and explain the inherited tolerances that lack a rationale.
CUDA and multi-rank results need their own provenance and cannot be inferred from a CPU algebra check.
